title: Hawaii’s ancient island origins explain why it has no native snakes
summary_full: Hawaii's unique volcanic history and geographic isolation effectively kept snakes from establishing themselves on the islands. This absence allowed native wildlife to flourish without the fear of snake predators. Unfortunately, accidental snake introductions, as evidenced by Guam's experiences, can wreak havoc. To combat this risk, Hawaii enforces strict regulations and vigilant monitoring to safeguard its delicate ecosystem and ensure the island's natural heritage endures.
